finding.summary: All-blank / mostly-blank bounded ranges now change results for AVERAGE/MEDIAN/STDEV/VAR/GEOMEAN (e.g. AVERAGE → #VALUE!), with no test for those functions
finding.evidence: With blanks skipped (arguments.ts:118-123), `averageFunc` reaches `count === 0` and returns `ErrNode.VALUE` (packages/sheets/src/formula/functions-statistical.ts:39-41) where it previously returned 0; `stdevFunc`/`varFunc` (639, 689) similarly flip to #VALUE! when fewer than two numeric cells survive. The only empty-data test added is `=SUM(A:A)` on an empty sheet → '0' (packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts:351-355). The repository has follow-up unit tests for MIN/MAX over blank ranges only (packages/sheets/test/formula/formula.test.ts:4412-4438) — nothing covers AVERAGE/MEDIAN/STDEV/VAR over an all-blank or single-numeric range, at either the formula or sheet level.

decision.reason: The diff does contain the described behavior change: arguments.ts now skips blank cells for ANY range reference (diff.patch:549-567, `isSrng(node.v)` + `continue` on `cell.v === undefined || ''`), which alters aggregation semantics for bounded ranges as well as the new unbounded forms. The added tests are accurately described by the reviewer: the only zero-numeric-data case is `=SUM(A:A)` on an empty sheet -> '0' (diff.patch:1125-1129), and the new formula-level block (diff.patch:998-1047) only covers lexing/rewriting plus one SUM evaluation. No test in this diff exercises AVERAGE/MEDIAN/STDEV/VAR/GEOMEAN over an all-blank (or single-numeric) range, where skipping blanks can flip the result from a number to an error. Partial mitigation exists: `AVERAGE(B2:B)` -> '200' (diff.patch:1082-1087) is genuine non-vacuous coverage of blank-skipping for AVERAGE (counting blanks would give 100), which suggests the severity may be closer to minor than major. However, I could not refute the finding on any named ground: the working directory /tmp/eval-item-hRoO8Z/repo is empty (Glob '**/*' returned nothing), so I could not read functions-statistical.ts to verify the claimed `count === 0 -> ErrNode.VALUE` path, nor search pre-existing test files for existing all-blank statistical coverage. Per the instructions, unresolved uncertainty keeps the finding.
